origin: Natural ignition; distinct from human-caused categories.
prevention: This is not generally preventable at ignition. Use local alerts, defensible-space practices, and emergency guidance to reduce exposure and consequences.
scope: NIFC distinguishes natural causes, generally lightning, from human activity. This guidance is not derived from FIRMS.

origin: Deliberate or malicious ignition; investigation establishes origin and cause.
prevention: Report unusual activity to authorities with dates, times, locations, and descriptions; do not confront suspects.
scope: Cause determination requires investigation; a satellite hotspot cannot establish arson.

origin: Escaped burn piles, burn barrels, yard debris, and other open burns.
prevention: Check local permits and restrictions; clear combustibles around small piles; keep water and a shovel nearby; attend until fully out; avoid unsafe wind/dry conditions.
scope: NIFC guidance includes a 4 ft maximum pile diameter and 10 ft clearance; local law and conditions govern.

origin: Vehicles, engines, tools, hot work, dragging metal, exhaust, or mechanical failure.
prevention: Maintain equipment; secure trailer chains; check tires, brakes, and dragging parts; follow local restrictions during fire danger.
scope: Examples and maintenance guidance summarized from NIFC.

origin: Projectiles, hot fragments, exploding targets, flares, and incendiary/tracer ammunition.
prevention: Check restrictions; avoid prohibited ammunition/exploding targets; place targets on dirt or gravel away from vegetation; carry water or an extinguisher.
scope: NIFC describes ignition pathways and jurisdiction-dependent restrictions.

origin: Ground, handheld, aerial, and explosive fireworks can send hot material into vegetation.
prevention: Follow local law and fire restrictions; fireworks may be prohibited on public lands or during high danger; use only where legal.
scope: Legal restrictions vary by location and date; consult local authorities.

origin: Includes fires started by children and adolescents.
prevention: Supervise children; store matches and lighters out of reach; teach that ignition tools are not toys; contact fire professionals if fire-setting behavior occurs.
scope: NIFC prevention guidance; not a prediction about individuals.

origin: Arcing, equipment failure, vegetation contact, and power-line events.
prevention: Stay away from lines and electrical equipment; report vegetation contact to the utility; leave clearance and maintenance work to professionals.
scope: NIFC advises professional maintenance and utility notification.

origin: Hot work, rail grinding, equipment, exhaust, brakes, derailment, and right-of-way work.
prevention: Rail operators and work crews should use fire prevention procedures and investigate/report ignition incidents; NIFC links to NWCG investigation training.
scope: Summary of NIFC classification; operational controls depend on rail authority and conditions.

origin: Improperly built, unattended, abandoned, or incompletely extinguished campfires and related devices.
prevention: Check restrictions; clear a 10 ft radius; keep adult supervision, water, and shovel; extinguish with “drown, stir & feel” until cool.
scope: CAL FIRE page gives campfire guidance for California; rules differ elsewhere.

origin: Discarded cigarettes, matches, cigars, and other smoking materials.
prevention: Check local restrictions; use only permitted cleared areas when restrictions allow; fully extinguish and dispose of materials safely.
scope: NIFC notes restrictions vary by jurisdiction and fire stage.

origin: NIFC examples include electric fences, glass refraction, spontaneous heating, and structures.
prevention: Maintain ignition-capable equipment; keep dry vegetation away from electrical equipment; safely manage oily rags/organic piles; supervise magnifying tools around children.
scope: NIFC “other” examples are heterogeneous; each requires cause-specific investigation and prevention.
